name: OWASP Amass
what: An OWASP attack-surface and asset discovery toolkit. Its strongest day-to-day use is subdomain and related asset enumeration from OSINT sources, with optional active techniques when you are allowed to probe the target.
when: At the start of an external assessment or continuous exposure program to build the inventory of domains and subdomains that belong to your organization before you scan them.
example: Install from the OWASP Amass releases or your package manager on an assessment host.
Passive enumeration first: `amass enum -passive -d contoso.com -o amass-passive.txt`.
With approval for active checks, run a fuller enum and compare against DNS and certificate inventory.
Feed confirmed in-scope hosts into Nuclei, Nmap or your vulnerability scanner; drop anything not yours.
pitfalls: Passive mode still queries third-party APIs; configure API keys responsibly and respect their terms.
Active mode can include techniques that touch the target; keep it inside the signed scope.
Results include noise and third-party SaaS hostnames; verify ownership before scanning.
